auth_details: Optional. Public SODA reads work without credentials. A free Socrata app token (X-App-Token header or $$app_token query param) is not authentication; it identifies the app for a higher request pool vs low anonymous IP throttling. OAuth/user auth is separate and only needed for private/write access.
rate_limits: Without app token: much lower IP-based throttling (exact threshold unpublished). With app token: substantially higher application-scoped limits; requests are generally unthrottled except under abuse/malicious traffic. Historical ~1,000 req/hour figures are not current official docs.
resolution_notes: auth.type: auditor correct. Official docs state app tokens are "not necessarily used for authentication" and unauthenticated public queries work without a token (https://dev.socrata.com/docs/app-tokens.html). Schema has no separate "optionalAppToken" type; "none" + details matches that model. rate_limits: auditor correct on removing ~1,000/hour. Same page documents lower IP throttling without token and higher limits with token, but publishes no numeric quota; changelog only clarified abuse handling (https://dev.socrata.com/docs/app-tokens.html, https://dev.socrata.com/changelog/2016/06/04/clarification-of-throttling-limits). example.request: auditor correct. Double-quoted URL causes shells to expand $limit; single-quote the URL (or escape $) so the SODA $limit param is sent.
